title: 1982 AHSME Problem 30
statement: Find the units digit in the decimal expansion of \[ (15+\sqrt{220})^{19}+(15+\sqrt{220})^{82}. \]

solutions.text:
Let \(\alpha=15+\sqrt{220}\) and \(\beta=15-\sqrt{220},\) so \(0\lt\beta\lt1.\) The integers \(S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n\) satisfy \(S_n=30S_{n-1}-5S_{n-2},\) hence \(S_n\equiv0\pmod{10}\) for every \(n\ge1.\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} \alpha^{19}+\alpha^{82} &=S_{19}+S_{82}\\ &\quad-(\beta^{19}+\beta^{82}) \end{aligned} \] is a multiple of \(10\) minus a positive number less than \(1.\) Its integer part therefore ends in \(9.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: The integers \(S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n\) satisfy a short recurrence, while \(0\lt\beta\lt1\)
